summary: Every concurrent vendor assertion in the elaborated closure is guarded by `ifndef VERILATOR and therefore did not execute in any RIFT simulation. Vendor elaboration-time initial assertions are compiled because Verilator ignores translate_off pragmas; they hold for all RIFT configurations and leave no residual runtime code. RIFT does not claim that vendor assertions executed and passed. RIFT's own boundary monitors are listed in docs/monitor_inventory.md and are counted per run.

items.name: initial assert(!(LockIn && ExtPrio))
items.note: THE LockIn/ExtPrio CONFLICT: xbar passes LockIn=1 unconditionally while bfly_net instantiates xbar with ExtPrio=1. With ExtPrio=1 rr_arb_tree takes the gen_ext_rr branch, so the LockIn branch is not elaborated. Under a non-Verilator frontend this assertion would reject the BFLY4 configuration. RIFT preserves the source unmodified and records the exclusion; any alternative simulator/formal frontend requires an explicit disposition before its results are accepted.

items.name: lock: LockIn |-> req_o && (!gnt_i && !flush_i) |=> idx_o == $past(idx_o)
items.note: inside gen_lock; elaborated only for LIC

items.name: lock_req: assume property (unserved requests not deasserted)
items.note: RIFT checks the equivalent driver obligation with monitor C1_REQUEST_STABILITY

disposition: No vendor source was patched. No global assertion disable was used (--assert is on). RIFT's acceptance relies on its own counted monitors and independent event checking, not on vendor assertion counts.
